en_alt: The officer gave an order to the soldiers.
note: Russian has no articles, so the indefinite reading is equally valid for the word-bank drill.

en_alt: The soldiers listen to the officer.
note: Imperfective present maps to both the simple and the continuous in English.

en_alt: The waitress brought us a menu.
note: Article choice is free here.

en_alt: The hunters built a campfire.
note: «костёр» is glossed campfire; the alt keeps the gloss visible while en_gb stays natural.

ru: Мы обрати́лись к охра́не за по́мощью.
en: We turned to security for help.
note: English 'the security' as a collective body takes no article.

en_alt: Security is standing at the gate.
The security guards are standing at the gate.
note: 'The security stands' is not English; the collective noun goes bare.

en_alt: We asked the security guard the way.
note: «спросить дорогу» is literally 'ask the way'.

ru: Но́чью в магази́не дежу́рят два охра́нника.

en_alt: He received an excellent mark.
note: «получить» is equally 'receive'.

en_alt: I joined the queue for the till.
note: «в кассу» is accusative — the queue is *for* the till.

en: Long queues formed at the entrance.
en_alt: Long queues gathered at the entrance.
note: Queues 'form' in English; 'gathered' collocates with people, not queues.

ru: В тёмных очка́х он похо́ж на настоя́щего шпио́на.

en_alt: I cannot see without glasses.
I can't see without my glasses.
note: Contraction and possessive are both free here.

en_alt: He wears reading glasses.
note: Idiomatic equivalent of «очки для чтения».

ru: Он вы́играл всего́ на одно́ очко́.
en_alt: He won by only one point.
note: «всего» is 'only' as readily as 'just'.

ru: О чужи́х оши́бках су́дят стро́же, чем о свои́х.
en_alt: Other people's mistakes are judged more harshly than one's own.
note: The impersonal plural «судят» is naturally a passive in English; the alt keeps that reading available.

ru: На свои́х оши́бках лю́ди у́чатся ме́дленно.
en_alt: People learn slowly from their own mistakes.
note: Adverb placement is free.

en_alt: It turned out to be a mistake.
note: «Это» renders as both 'that' and 'it'.

en_alt: The teacher finds mistakes quickly.
note: Adverb position and the bare plural are both valid.

en_alt: He was carrying a bag with the shopping.
note: «с покупками» is literally 'with the shopping'.

en_alt: We put up the tent by the river.
note: «поставить» is literally 'put up'.

ru: Пиани́ст едва́ каса́лся кла́виш то́нкими па́льцами.

en_alt: He pointed to the map with his finger.
note: 'point at' and 'point to' are both fine for «указать на».

en_alt: There are ten fingers on two hands.
note: 'on the hands' is slightly stilted; the alt reads more naturally without adding a person.

en_alt: The children collected sticks for the campfire.
note: «костёр» is glossed campfire and «собирать» is 'collect'.

en_alt: The old man was leaning on a stick.
note: «опирался» is imperfective, so the continuous is equally right.

en_alt: The pilgrims are walking to the holy place.
note: «идут» is determinate motion in progress; the continuous is the closer reading.

ru: Она́ наде́ла пальто́ и вы́шла на у́лицу.
en_alt: She put on her coat and went out into the street.
note: «на улицу» is literally 'into the street'.

ru: Зимо́й он хо́дит в тёплом пальто́.

en_alt: She doesn't have a winter coat.
note: Both negation patterns are equally natural.

en_alt: The tourists photograph the monument.
note: Imperfective present covers both English presents.

ru: Он де́лает э́то в па́мять о дру́ге.
У неё хоро́шая па́мять на лица́.
Э́та пе́сня оста́лась в па́мяти навсегда́.
en_alt: This song remained in the memory forever.
note: «осталась» is equally 'remained'.

ru: Все па́пы пришли́ на шко́льный спекта́кль.

en_alt: Dad, help me with my lessons!
note: «уроки» is glossed 'lesson'; the alt keeps that reading available alongside the idiomatic 'homework'.

en_alt: The old man lit up a papirosa.
note: «закурил» is literally 'lit up'.

en_alt: There are different folders on the shelf.
note: «разные» is glossed 'different'.
«пара» is 'pair' in this counting sense; the headword gloss 'couple' is narrower than the word, worth noting but the sentence is right.

en_alt: A young couple is walking around the park.
note: «по парку» is motion around/through the park.

en_alt: Two couples were sitting at the table.
note: «сидели» is imperfective, so the continuous is the closer reading.
Stress error: the nominative plural of па́рень is па́рни (end stress only from the genitive plural парне́й onwards).

en_alt: We are going to Paris in summer.
note: Article before 'summer' is optional.

en_alt: She returned from Paris.
note: The Russian past is equally the simple past in English.

ru: Ря́дом с до́мом два больши́х па́рка.
en_alt: There are two big parks next to the house.
note: «большой» is glossed 'big' and «рядом с» is 'next to'.

ru: В городски́х па́рках о́сенью па́хнет опа́вшими ли́стьями.

en_alt: The car park is round the corner.
note: 'round the corner' is the commoner British form.

ru: Я не нашёл ме́ста на парко́вке.
en_alt: I did not find a space in the car park.
note: «место» is 'space' as well as 'spot' in a car park.
The collocation is «участвовать в выборах», and «много» + inanimate genitive takes a singular verb: участвует, not участвуют.

en_alt: The party members gathered in the hall.
note: Both genitive and attributive renderings are natural.

en_alt: All the passengers boarded the train.
note: «сели в поезд» is equally 'boarded'.

en_alt: For dinner I cooked pasta.
note: «приготовила» is glossed 'to prepare; to cook'.

en_alt: There is a lot of sauce in the pasta.
note: Uncontracted form for the word-bank drill.

en_alt: There were few cartridges left in the box.
note: «осталось» is equally 'were left'.

en_alt: Two spiders were sitting in the corner.
note: «сидели» is imperfective, so the continuous is the closer reading.

en_alt: The spider weaves a web.
note: Imperfective present covers both English presents.

en: This paella has seafood in it.
en_alt: This paella is with seafood.
This is a seafood paella.
note: 'X is with Y' is translationese; English states the contents.

en_alt: There is a big choice of dumplings in the shop.
note: The entry mixes 'pelmeni' and 'dumpling' across its sentences; the alt keeps the headword gloss usable.

en_alt: For dinner we boiled dumplings.
note: Keeps the headword gloss usable alongside the transliteration.

en_alt: They gave the pensioner a discount on the ticket.
note: The impersonal plural «дали» renders as either a passive or an indefinite 'they'.
«на пенсии» genuinely means 'in retirement'; the sentence is right even though it diverges from the headword gloss.

en_alt: Grandfather will retire soon.
note: «выйти на пенсию» is simply 'to retire'; 'retire on a pension' adds a claim the Russian does not make and is not idiomatic.

«прийти к переговорам» is an odd collocation — Russian says «приступи́ли к перегово́рам» (began negotiations) or «пришли́ к соглаше́нию»; the English 'came to negotiations' is awkward for the same reason, so a human should pick which side to change.

en_alt: The negotiations continued all day.
note: «продолжались» is literally 'continued'.

en_alt: There are many new programmes on television.
note: 'programme' is the natural English for a TV «передача»; the headword gloss 'broadcast' may be too narrow.

en_alt: We talked about an interesting programme.
note: Same 'programme' reading as the entry's other sentences.

ru: Моя́ люби́мая переда́ча начина́ется в во́семь.
en_alt: My favourite programme starts at eight.
note: Same 'programme' reading; 'starts' is equally natural for «начинается».

en_alt: The doctor treated the broken arm.
note: Natural English prefers 'broken arm'; en_gb keeps the literal reading.

en_alt: He has a broken leg.
note: 'a fracture of the leg' is stilted in ordinary speech; the alt gives the idiomatic reading without losing the literal en_gb.
The English is correct — «на перемене» is the school break — but the headword gloss 'change' does not cover that sense, so the gloss is probably what needs widening.

en_alt: A big change took place in life.
note: «произошла» renders as both 'occurred' and 'took place'.

en_alt: We are ready for change.
note: English 'change' is often uncountable here.

ru: По́сле переры́ва мы верну́лись к рабо́те.
en_alt: After the break we returned to work.
note: «вернулись» is literally 'returned'.

en_alt: Let's have a break.
note: Both 'take' and 'have' a break are natural British English.

en_alt: There are many underpasses in the city.
note: «подземный переход» is an underpass; en_gb keeps the literal reading for the gloss.
